summary: Manitoba's highest point; one of the first fire lookout towers was built here in the early 1900s, and a 12 m observation tower stands on the summit today.

facts.design: Built of poles cut nearby, per a 1915 report; the tower standing today is a 12 m observation tower

access.note: Visitors can drive to the top of the mountain, per the Manitoba park sheet. The site is on Provincial Road 366, 32 km north of Grandview.

visit.trail_note: Trail begins at a parking area near the summit, about 2 km in total and mostly paved. The stairs can be icy in early spring and late autumn.

events.note: Earliest dated record. A 1915 forestry report describes the tower as already built, so it may be older. The Manitoba park sheet dates one of the first towers on the mountain to the early 1900s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Manitoba park sheet dates one of the first towers to the early 1900s. A 1915 forestry report already describes the tower as built. The story gives both and does not name a single build year.

notes_for_editor: The brief's agency (Manitoba Conservation / Parks) is not named in any page read, so no agency fact is recorded. The pages do not say whether the 12 m observation tower on the summit is the original pole tower or a later one, so the story does not claim either. No staffing or fire evidence was found in two searches and six reads. Height 12 m is the current viewing tower, not the 1915 structure.
